Lancaster County at a glance

Lancaster County spans about 846 square miles, and Lincoln is its seat and Nebraska's capital. Bennet, Hickman, Lincoln and Waverly are the cities. Villages include Davey, Denton, Firth, Hallam, Malcolm, Panama, Raymond, Roca and Sprague. One sale might be a house in Lincoln, an acreage near Branched Oak Lake or a village home in Hallam, and the same county offices handle all three.

The 2020 census counted 322,608 residents and 135,484 housing units, 5.6% vacant. Few owner-occupied homes sat empty, since the homeowner vacancy rate was 1.0 percent. Renters lived in more than four in ten occupied homes, so a house with a tenant is a familiar sale. Roughly nine in ten residents live in urban areas, which means most deals involve city lots rather than farm ground.

Delinquent dates and where to pay

Taxes are due December 31. Nebraska statute 77-204 treats a county of more than 100,000 residents differently: the first half is late after April 1 and the second after August 1. A first-half payment that would be fine under a May 1 calendar is already late here.

Your bank or a bill payment service can send real estate and personal property payments electronically. The treasurer's property search lists the rate and tax district for each parcel. Rates vary by district, so look up the parcel you're selling instead of guessing a countywide number. The same treasurer collects for schools, fire districts, cities and villages.

How to protest a valuation

The County Clerk accepts Form 422 only from June 1 through June 30. Anything that arrives early or is postmarked late gets rejected as untimely.

State the property description and your reason. The County Board of Equalization hears it. If you lose, you have 30 days after the board adjourns to appeal to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission. The Assessor/Register of Deeds is one elected office with general supervision over assessment of all property in the county, phone (402) 441-8776.

Rulings on protests can trickle out well past June, yet the window to file is only 30 days. Gather photographs, repair quotes and nearby sales before June 1 so you aren't scrambling.

Tax checks before closing

Given the early April and August dates, timing is the main risk. Run these checks:

  • Search the parcel on the treasurer's property information site and confirm both halves of last year's bill are paid.
  • Find out from the closing agent if the current-year bill comes entirely out of your proceeds or is shared with the buyer.
  • Verify the mailing address on file, because statements go to the address on the transfer statement filed with the deed.

Treat the online figure as a starting point and get the payoff in writing before closing.

Storms are a regular risk for roofs, so expect questions about roof age and earlier claims. Keep those details handy.

Recording the deed

The Register of Deeds, 555 South 10th Street in Lincoln, records deeds for $10.00 on page one and $6.00 for each page after. Each deed travels with a completed Real Estate Transfer Statement (Form 521) and the documentary stamp tax where it applies.

Staff suggest emailing a copy to RegDeed@lancaster.ne.gov before you mail the original, so they can review recordability and fees. Electronic recording runs through contracted vendors. The county charges nothing extra for e-filing, but each vendor sets a fee. Call 402-441-7463; staff can't fill out documents or give legal advice.

The forms page includes the Certificate of Exemption from the documentary stamp tax (form 5b). For deeds recorded from July 18, 2026 the state rate is $3.32 on every $1,000 of value, owed by the seller as grantor.

Before you list: a short checklist

Paperwork on hand makes a sale quicker. Start with this pile.

  1. Your latest tax statement and a printout from the treasurer's property search.
  2. Proof that the prior year's two halves are paid, or a written payoff if either is open.
  3. The deed, with the mailing address you want on future statements.
  4. Roof age and any prior storm claims.
  5. Lease and tenant details, if someone lives in the house.
  6. Photos and quotes if you plan to protest next June.

A title company can work from this list to confirm payoffs and prepare Form 521. A missing item is the usual reason a closing slips.

How a closing unfolds, step by step

Once you have a buyer, the sequence in Lancaster County runs the same way whether the sale is financed or cash.

  1. The title company opens an order and looks up the parcel on the treasurer's site.
  2. It requests payoff figures, including any December 31 bill that is current, and compares them with your own printout.
  3. You and the buyer agree in writing how the current-year bill is split.
  4. The deed and Form 521 are prepared, with the documentary stamp tax figured as the seller's cost.
  5. A copy goes to the Register of Deeds by email for a recordability check, and the original is recorded for the page fees.
  6. The treasurer's records update, and future statements follow the mailing address given on the transfer statement.

Each step is simple on its own. Trouble comes when two of them collide, such as a payoff that was never refreshed or a deed missing its transfer statement.

If a tenant lives in the house

More than four in ten occupied homes here are rented, so many sellers face this. A cash buyer may take the house with the tenant still living there, so you needn't ask anyone to leave before closing. Taxes work as always: the same bill, the same dates and a payoff confirmed by the title company. Keep the lease, the rent record and the tenant's contact details together so the buyer and title company can read them quickly. Tell the tenant early that a sale is underway, and share any inspection dates as soon as you know them.

Frequently asked questions

When are Lancaster County property taxes delinquent?

Late dates are April 1 for the first half and August 1 for the second, set by Nebraska statute 77-204 for counties over 100,000 residents.

What is the Lancaster County protest period?

Form 422 goes to the County Clerk, who accepts it June 1 through June 30 only.

Where is the Lancaster County treasurer's office?

Go to 555 S. 10th Street, Room 102, Lincoln, any weekday between 7:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. A bank's bill payment service also works.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Lancaster County?

Page one costs $10.00 and each added page $6.00. You also need Form 521 and any documentary stamp tax, which is $3.32 on every $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

Is the Lancaster County tax rate the same across the county?

No. The rate depends on the tax district, and the treasurer's property search shows it for each parcel.

Gage County at a glance

Beatrice is the seat of Gage County, which borders Kansas on Nebraska's southern edge. Population has held steady: 21,704 at the 2020 census and an estimated 21,711 in 2025. The county has three cities, Beatrice, Blue Springs and Wymore, plus nine villages. Lincoln is the nearest large city for much of the county, about 40 miles north of Beatrice.

Housing units numbered 10,327 in 2020, with 10.1% vacant. Renters occupied nearly three in ten homes, so landlords make up a real share of sellers. A county settled this early describes parcels by legal description, and a title company will want to read that description and the recorded history before closing.

How the assessor values a home

For most homes the assessor starts from replacement cost new, subtracts depreciation, adds land, and then checks the result against sales within set market areas. Residential and commercial values aim for 92 to 100 percent of market value, and agricultural land for 69 to 75 percent.

Residential values rely on a two-year sales study, agricultural and commercial values on three years, and the study period ends June 30 of the preceding year. State law has the office review each property at least every six years. Field staff drive county vehicles and wear name badges and bright green vests.

  • A market neighborhood can include as many as 500 homes, so values are set by group, not by one sale.
  • Commercial property is often valued by an income approach, and income information sent to the office stays confidential.
  • Statements go to the address on line 19 of the Form 521 transfer statement filed with your deed.
  • Greenbelt status for qualifying farmland requires Form 456 before August 1.
  • Ask the assessor's office which market area your house falls in, since that group's sales drive the value.

Protesting a valuation

You protest the valuation, never the tax itself. Form 422, in triplicate, goes to the County Board of Equalization through the county clerk's office at 612 Grant Street in Beatrice. Real property protests are due on or before June 30 and personal property protests by May 1. A protest that omits the requested value and the reasons can be dismissed.

The assessor's office suggests first asking an appraiser to explain how your value was reached, which gives the office a chance to fix errors. After a hearing, the board notifies you of its decision within seven days. If you still disagree, the Tax Equalization and Review Commission hears an appeal filed within 30 days of the board's adjournment; July 25 counts as that date for the June 1 to July 25 session.

What helps is a showing that your value sits above the market or out of step with similar properties.

Tax due dates and ways to pay

Both real estate and personal property bills are due December 31, and notices go out in December. Half becomes delinquent on May 1 of the next year and the rest on September 1, with delinquencies charged a 14 percent statutory rate.

The treasurer's office phone is (402) 223-1319. A wrong address can be fixed by phone or with the county's change of address form.

Mobile homes follow a few extra rules. The county doesn't prorate taxes on a sold mobile home, so buyer and seller must split them. A moving permit isn't issued until taxes are paid to date, and moving without that step is a class four misdemeanor. If the new owner never files forms 521 and 402, the tax statement stays in the seller's name.

How the Gage County tax sale works

Each March the treasurer runs a public tax sale at 9:00 a.m. in the third-floor district courtroom. The Beatrice Daily Sun carries the delinquent parcels for three consecutive weeks in February beforehand.

Bidders register in advance, pay a $25 registration fee, and take turns choosing parcels round-robin under Nebraska statute 77-1807. A buyer gets a tax lien, not the property. A certificate that isn't redeemed within three years opens the way to foreclosure, with strict notice deadlines before three years and nine months. Redemption pays the buyer 14 percent interest, and purchasers add an automatic $150 administrative fee for serving notice on the owner, which the owner pays at redemption.

Bankruptcy parcels and government-owned land never go to the sale. Owners who want to avoid the notice step and extra fees usually clear the balance or sell before the February advertising run.

Exemptions, recording and permits

Homestead exemption applicants, generally owners over 65 and certain disabled people, must file between February 1 and June 30 every year in the assessor's office. You lose the exemption if you sell or leave the home before August 15, though if you buy another Nebraska home before that date you can file a transfer statement to move it.

Closing brings the state documentary stamp tax: $3.32 on every $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026, owed by the seller as grantor. Zoning and building permits, including setbacks, are checked by legal description and address with county planning, and a permit application needs two identical sets of plans.

Added a garage, deck or finished space? Collect the permits before you list, since a title company or lender may ask.

Before you list: a short checklist

  • Call the treasurer for your balance and ask whether the parcel is headed for the February advertising list.
  • Check which half of the bill is open, remembering the May 1 and September 1 delinquency dates.
  • Confirm that forms 521 and 402 were filed when you bought, so the statement and mailing address are right.
  • Collect permits for any addition, garage or deck.
  • If you claim a homestead exemption, remember it ends if you sell before August 15 unless you transfer it to another Nebraska home.
  • For a mobile home, settle with the buyer in writing how the taxes are split, since the county won't prorate them.

Sellers who work through this list usually learn the payoff figure before they talk to any buyer, and that makes comparing offers far easier.

Selling a Gage County house with taxes owed

A house on the tax sale list can still be sold if the delinquent taxes and charges are cleared at closing. Where a certificate has already been bought, redemption adds the buyer's interest and the $150 service fee. Your title company gets the payoff from the treasurer and deducts it from your proceeds.

Send Cash Home Buyers a Gage County address and we'll explain how an as-is offer would work. There are no showings or lender appraisals, which helps when the February advertising date is near. Ask the treasurer's office at (402) 223-1319 for the balance before you call us, if you can.

Frequently asked questions

When are Gage County property taxes due?

December 31. The first half is delinquent the following May 1 and the second half the following September 1, with a 14 percent statutory rate on delinquencies.

Can I protest my Gage County property tax bill?

Only the valuation, not the bill. Send Form 422 to the county clerk in Beatrice by June 30 for real property, naming the value you want and your reasons.

What fees apply when paying Gage County taxes by card?

Cards carry a 2.49 percent convenience fee and e-checks cost $1.75. Pay online at nto.us.

Does Gage County prorate taxes when a mobile home is sold?

No. Buyer and seller divide them. The new owner also files forms 521 and 402 with the assessor, or the statement keeps the seller's name.

Can I sell a Gage County house that is on the tax sale list?

Yes, once delinquent taxes and charges are cleared at closing. When a certificate was already sold, redemption also costs the buyer's interest and a $150 service fee.

Saunders County at a glance

Saunders County covers about 760 square miles of eastern Nebraska, and Wahoo is both the county seat and the largest city. The county counts as part of the Omaha-Council Bluffs metropolitan area, yet most of its land is farm ground, in low rolling hills that slope toward the Platte River valley on the north and east.

The 2020 census counted 22,278 residents. Wahoo had 4,818, Ashland 3,086 and Yutan 1,347. Villages include Ceresco, Mead, Cedar Bluffs, Valparaiso, Memphis, Prague and Weston, and 9,045 people, about 41 percent of the county, live outside any town. There were 9,987 housing units in 2020, with 79.6% owner-occupied.

That 41 percent matters when you sell. Plenty of Saunders County homes sit on acreage outside a city limit, where wells, zoning and road questions differ from a lot in Wahoo.

Which offices handle property tax

Three offices share the courthouse at 433 N Chestnut, Wahoo, NE 68066, and each does a different job. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

  • Assessor (Suite 200, 402-443-5600) values every parcel in the county.
  • Treasurer (Suite 201, 402-443-8128, mail to PO Box 337) bills and collects real estate and personal property tax and passes the money to schools, cities and other districts. A new title has to be in the door by 4:00 p.m. The same office handles motor vehicle registration and driver licensing.
  • Register of Deeds (Suite 203, 402-443-8111) records deeds and mortgages. Deeds from 1997 forward can be searched on Nebraska Deeds Online.

You can also pay through the state's Nebraska Taxes Online page for Saunders County.

How the assessor values a property

Value is set as of 12:01 a.m. on January 1 each tax year. Homes, commercial property and industrial property are valued at 100 percent of market value, and agricultural and horticultural land at 75 percent. State section 77-201 sets the 75 percent rule for farmland, with a lower 50 percent figure for school bond levies approved by voters on or after January 1, 2022.

The assessor only sets the value. The rate comes from the county board and every other taxing body, and it is applied to that value. If you disagree with a value, you work through the protest window handled by the county board, not through the Treasurer.

Levy figures

In the 2024 data, the county's own levy was $0.2160 per $100 of taxable valuation. It raised about $12.0 million of the roughly $75.6 million that all local governments levied, so the county board's slice is about 16 percent of what property owners pay in total.

Schools, the city or village, the natural resource district and other bodies add their own levies, so the county line is never the whole bill. The Department of Revenue posts every rate in its annual taxing subdivisions report.

Why similar houses pay different tax

The county is cut into many school districts and village limits, and each combination carries its own total levy. Thirteen school districts serve parts of the county, among them Ashland-Greenwood, Wahoo, Yutan, Mead, Cedar Bluffs, Raymond Central and North Bend Central, plus districts named for Fremont, Gretna, Schuyler, Waverly and David City. Lower Platte North and Lower Platte South are the two natural resource districts that reach in.

A buyer comparing a Wahoo address with an Ashland address, or a town lot with an acreage, should ask for the actual prior-year bill, not a county average. Electric providers also vary by location: Butler PPD, the City of Wahoo, Omaha PPD and the Village of Prague. That is a useful line in a listing or a cash-offer conversation about monthly carrying costs.

What changes at closing

The seller pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax, and the title company settles the current year's property tax between the two sides. Under section 76-901 the tax falls on the grantor at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for transfers before January 1, 2032, then drops to $2.32. Value means the full consideration, including any liens the buyer assumes, and a fraction of $1,000 counts as a full $1,000.

Deeds between spouses, between ex-spouses dividing marital property, or between parent and child with no actual payment are exempt under section 76-902(5)(a). Families passing a house down should confirm the exemption wording with the Register of Deeds before recording.

  • Ask the title company for a written tax proration before you sign.
  • Check that every delinquent installment is in the payoff figures.
  • Record the deed in Wahoo, then confirm the Assessor has the new owner's mailing address.

The Register of Deeds also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails an owner when a document is recorded under their name. It is worth setting up for any house that will sit vacant before a sale.

Selling an acreage or farmstead

Check water, zoning and land classification first, because a farmstead is valued and regulated differently from a town lot. The county counts 1,500 rural drinking water wells, and state law does not require registration of small wells drilled before September 9, 1993, so a missing record is not unusual for an older place.

  • Wells that can pump more than 50 gallons a minute must be registered and permitted through the local natural resource district.
  • Saunders County is a zoned county, so ask before assuming a land split or second dwelling is allowed.
  • Dryland crop ground covers 51 percent of the county's land and irrigated ground 23 percent, and the mix on a parcel affects its farm valuation.

Nebraska's seller disclosure law, section 76-2,120, asks sellers of one-to-four-unit residential property to state the condition of the electrical, heating, water and sewer systems in writing. A fiduciary selling for an estate is generally excused unless that person lived in the home.

Step by step if you want to sell

A short checklist keeps a Saunders County sale moving.

  • Call the Treasurer for the payoff and any open installment.
  • Look up the recorded deed on Nebraska Deeds Online so your name and legal description match.
  • If the place is an acreage, gather what you know about the well and any zoning approvals.
  • Fill out the written condition statement honestly, marking an item unknown only if it truly is.
  • Ask the title company for the tax proration in writing before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Saunders County property tax?

Pay the Treasurer at 433 N Chestnut, Suite 201, in Wahoo, mail to PO Box 337, or use Nebraska Taxes Online. The office phone is 402-443-8128.

How do I find a recorded deed in Saunders County?

Deeds from 1997 to the present are searchable on Nebraska Deeds Online. For older records, call the Register of Deeds at 402-443-8111, Suite 203 of the Wahoo courthouse.

Do I owe stamp tax if I deed my house to my child?

Not if no actual payment changes hands. Nebraska exempts deeds between parent and child without actual consideration under section 76-902(5)(a). A sale at a stated price is taxed at $3.32 per $1,000 before 2032.

Is farmland assessed the same as a house in Saunders County?

No. The Assessor values homes and commercial property at 100 percent of market value and agricultural and horticultural land at 75 percent, as of January 1.

Who pays the current year's tax when a Saunders County house sells mid-year?

The purchase contract and the title company decide how the year is split. Ask for the proration in writing, and make sure any delinquent installment is paid from your proceeds at closing.

Cass County at a glance

Cass County, Nebraska, runs along the Platte River on its north side and the Missouri River on its east, with Plattsmouth as the county seat and largest city. The Assessor values more than 21,000 real estate parcels. Knowing which office does what saves a lot of phone calls once a sale is underway.

Which office does what

The Assessor values property and the Treasurer collects the tax. The Assessor's office is in the Annex at 145 N. 4th St., just north of the courthouse at the corner of N. 4th St. and Avenue A. It's open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 4:30 p.m., phone 402-296-9310.

The Treasurer's page shows the office at 446 Main Street, 2nd floor, with the same weekday hours and a property tax line at 402-296-9511. The office has moved recently, so confirm the location before you bring a payment.

  • The counter takes cash, check, money order and cards (extra fees apply).
  • Online payments go through Nebraska Taxes Online at nto.us.
  • Cards can't be used for tax sale redemptions.

On the valuation side, the Assessor handles about 1,300 personal property parcels, processes over 900 homestead applications and 150 permissive exemption applications, and answers about 10,000 information requests a year.

Delinquency dates and interest

Delinquent Cass County tax turns late on May 1 and September 1. Check the statement for the county that sends it, since each Nebraska county sets its own calendar in practice.

The rate on delinquent tax comes from state law. When an owner redeems after a tax sale, the buyer of the certificate receives 14% simple interest from the sale date to the redemption date.

The 2026 reappraisal

  • Towns: Avoca, Manley, Nehawka, Union and Weeping Water villages
  • Rural townships: Mount Pleasant, Center, Weeping Water, Avoca/Nehawka and Nehawka/Liberty

Collectors wear orange reflective vests, carry county badges issued by the Sheriff's Office and drive county vehicles. They photograph and measure structures. If nobody's home, they leave a call-back slip on the door. Owners can return a property review questionnaire by mail or in the drop box on the west side of the courthouse.

If you own in one of those areas and plan to sell, use the visit to confirm that the square footage, finished basement and outbuildings on record match what's really there. Errors in that record affect the value your buyer will be taxed on.

Fillmore County at a glance

Geneva is the county seat and the only city in Fillmore County, in southeastern Nebraska. Exeter, Fairmont, Grafton, Milligan, Ohiowa, Shickley and Strang are villages. Residents numbered 5,551 at the 2020 census and an estimated 5,458 in 2025, a small and slowly shrinking population. Corn and soybeans drive the farm economy.

The 2020 count found 2,718 housing units, 12.2% of them vacant. With that much empty stock, a house that needs work can sit on the market for months. If you hold a vacant inherited home or an unwanted rental, the wait has to be weighed against another year of taxes and upkeep.

Many houses and farmsteads go back to the 1870s, when the railroad arrived. On older property, buyers start with the roof, wiring and foundation. Low spots on the flat loess plain can pond after heavy rain or snowmelt, so look at drainage before you list.

Due dates and delinquency

Both real estate and personal property bills in Fillmore County are late after two dates, May 1 and September 1 (Nebraska statutes 77-203 and 77-204), and interest then runs at 14 percent. Tax notices are mailed around December 1.

Deadline or feeFillmore County rule

Paid receipts are no longer mailed automatically, so tuck a stamped, self-addressed envelope into your payment if you want one back. Amounts and status show on the Nebraska Taxes Online website, or you can phone the treasurer. If a notice never arrives, call the office anyway, since a missing notice doesn't move the due date. Moving? Phone the office or send the county's change of address form.

A house that sells early in the year may still owe the first half of the prior year's bill until May 1. Have the closing agent show which half is being paid and who is paying it.

Challenging your valuation

The thing you can contest is the valuation, never the tax bill. Nebraska Form 422, from the Department of Revenue, goes to the county clerk, whose staff run the County Board of Equalization. For real property the deadline is June 30.

A valid protest names the value you want and gives the reason. A losing party can go on to the state's Tax Equalization and Review Commission, but only within 30 days of the board's adjournment. For the June 1 to July 25 session, July 25 is deemed the adjournment date.

Convincing proof might be a recent sale of a comparable house nearby, a repair estimate that explains a lower condition, or proof that comparable properties carry lower values. When there's a failing roof, a cracked foundation or other major defect, photos and contractor bids outweigh opinion.

Rural acreage may be taxed as agricultural land, a different valuation track from a town lot.

When taxes go unpaid

If tax goes unpaid, the parcel can be sold as a lien at the treasurer's yearly auction. It takes place at the courthouse at 9:00 a.m. on the first Monday in March, and for three consecutive weeks in February the local paper and Nebraska Taxes Online carry the delinquent list.

A bidder buys a lien on the parcel, not the house. Owners have three years to redeem, the certificate earns 14 percent, and the buyer must keep paying later years' delinquent taxes to hold the certificate. Should three years pass without redemption, the holder then has six months to begin foreclosure.

February is therefore a real deadline. Closing before the list runs keeps your parcel out of print, and advertising costs get added to what a certificate buyer pays. County staff can't offer legal advice, so take certificate and redemption questions to a Nebraska attorney.

What the deed costs

Selling means paying the state's documentary stamp tax. From July 18, 2026 it's $3.32 on each $1,000 of value, rounding any fraction up to a full $1,000, and the seller as grantor is responsible. The deed must also carry a finished Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, or the register of deeds will send it back.

A few transfers are exempt, certain deeds to trustees among them. Both documents are normally drawn up by a title company or closing attorney, and the amount appears on your estimated settlement statement.

US 81 comes in from Thayer County and heads north into York County. US 6 crosses the north, Nebraska Highway 41 runs up the middle and Highway 74 follows the south. BNSF Railway tracks pass Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton.

What a closing looks like

A Fillmore County sale moves through a few hands. Early on, the closing agent asks the treasurer which half-year is open and how much interest has built up. The deed and Form 521 are drafted, and the stamp tax is listed on the settlement statement. When the sale closes, any delinquent balance is taken out of your proceeds and the deed is filed with the register of deeds.

If the house is on the tax sale list and a certificate has already been sold, ask the agent for the redemption figure, because it includes the buyer's interest. Questions about a tax lien or foreclosure deadline belong with a Nebraska attorney, not the county office.

Selling a Fillmore County house on a deadline

Inherited, behind on taxes or just worn out, the house can still sell. A few steps keep it moving:

  • Ask the treasurer or closing agent for the exact payoff and which half-year is open.
  • Choose between a June 30 protest or selling and leaving the next valuation to the buyer.
  • If the parcel is headed for the February advertising list, aim to close before it runs.
  • Have the title company prepare the deed and Form 521.

When are Fillmore County property taxes delinquent?

After May 1 and after September 1, when 14 percent interest starts. If April 30 or August 31 is a weekend or holiday, the following business day is still interest-free.

Where do I file a property valuation protest in Fillmore County?

Nebraska Form 422 goes to the county clerk, who handles the County Board of Equalization. Real property protests are due June 30 and must give the value you want and your reason.

Can I sell a Fillmore County house that has back taxes?

Yes. A payoff request goes from the closing agent to the treasurer, and the balance is deducted from what you receive. Closing before the February advertising run keeps your parcel off the public list.

Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Fillmore County sale?

The seller does, as grantor, unless an exemption fits. The charge is $3.32 on every $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

How can I check what I owe the Fillmore County treasurer?

Look up amounts and payment status on Nebraska Taxes Online, or call the treasurer's office through the county website.

Richardson County at a glance

Richardson County occupies the southeast corner of Nebraska. Missouri is across the river to the east and Kansas lies south, and the state's lowest point is where the Missouri leaves Nebraska. Parts of the Ioway and Sac and Fox reservations lie in the southeast corner, and the village of Preston is inside the Sac and Fox reservation. The 2020 census counted 7,871 residents. Median age was 47.2, and 24.9% of residents were 65 or older. An heir who lives out of state and inherits a house in Dawson, Stella or Verdon owes the same tax on the same dates as a neighbor.

Certificates are sold the first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse. The delinquent list is advertised for three consecutive weeks in February and posted online, and the county also posts a list of parcels that went unsold.

  • Check the assessor's record for the parcel, and ask about classification if it lies near reservation land.
  • See whether the parcel is on the county's list of unsold tax sale parcels.
  • Collect repair invoices and insurance claim papers so storm questions get plain answers.
  • Hand the title company the parcel number so payoff and deed are prepared together.

A brief call to each office usually shows which items apply to you.

When heirs inherit a house

Older owners mean some houses will move to heirs here. The tax calendar does not pause while an estate is settled, so May and September arrive on schedule for the heir too.

Be ready with papers showing who may sign, because the title company will ask. An heir in another state can handle most of this by phone and mail, since the treasurer, assessor and register of deeds all answer calls.

No lender means no bank appraisal and no loan committee. For a house with deferred repairs, that removes the most common reason a closing collapses.

The stamp tax and every tax balance, drainage taxes included, still get settled at closing. What you gain is a calendar that follows title work and the payoff, and often your choice of closing day.

Why drainage taxes need a separate call

Drainage taxes are the one item on a Richardson County bill that the online payment system will not accept. A seller who pays everything else online and forgets the drainage line can leave a small balance sitting open at closing.

Call the treasurer at 402-245-3511 and ask for a payoff that spells out the drainage items on their own line. Hand that figure to the title company, and the balance gets paid from your proceeds with everything else.

After each March sale, the county posts the parcels that found no buyer. Being on that list does not erase the debt. The first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse, after three weeks of advertising in February.

School districts, community colleges, cities, the county and natural resource districts each set a budget, so the district your house falls in changes its tax rate. The Assessor/Register of Deeds also watches sale prices, because every sale is recorded in the same office. Each price is compared with the last assessed value, and when prices in an area move a lot, a revaluation follows. A house that sells far from its assessment is a signal the office reads.

Who to call about property tax

Value, protests and collection sit with three separate offices: the Assessor/Register of Deeds, the Board of Equalization and the Treasurer.

  • Treasurer: (402) 444-7103, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; mail to PO Box 2855, Omaha, NE 68103.

Nebraska taxes are paid in arrears. In the Board of Equalization's words, the tax you pay in calendar year 2026 is your 2025 tax, based on your 2025 valuation. Your 2026 valuation affects the bill you pay in 2027, so a buyer inherits the next valuation, not the one on today's statement.

The grantor, the seller, is liable, though the buyer or any agent presenting the deed may pay it.

June 30. The formal protest period runs June 1 to June 30, and mailed protests need a June 30 postmark.

Red Willow County at a glance

Red Willow County hugs Nebraska's southern border, and McCook is where the courthouse stands. Indianola is the other city. After decades of slow loss, some owners would rather close quickly as-is than sit through a long listing. A vacant house still draws a tax bill, and it ages faster when nobody checks the roof, furnace and plumbing.

Who bills and collects the tax

Real estate tax is collected by the county treasurer at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook. Mail goes to PO Box 490, McCook, NE 69001, and the phone is 308-345-6515, extension 1. The state's tax portal shows current and back taxes and takes payment for both. A card costs 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check costs $2.00.

Next door in the same building, the assessor answers at 308-345-4388 or assessor@redwillowcountyne.gov, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with no lunch closure. What changes a valuation

The assessor lists four things that push a value up or down: movement in the market, outside influences on the property, improvements added or removed, and a remodel or rehab. A new garage or finished basement raises the number, and tearing down a tired outbuilding should lower it.

Exemptions exist for educational and religious facilities and for qualifying seniors and people with disabilities. Ask the assessor's office which one fits before you assume you owe the full amount.

How to appeal your assessment

A protest has to reach the County Clerk by June 30. Say what value you want and why. The clerk mails the board's decision by August 2, and the Tax Equalization and Review Commission accepts appeals until August 24.

Give the board something concrete: a recent appraisal, photos and a bid for needed repairs, or sale prices of similar houses nearby.

On the first Monday of March each year, the county sells certificates for unpaid real estate tax at the courthouse. The delinquent list is advertised in the local paper and online for three consecutive weeks in February.

  • Owners get three years to redeem, with the certificate earning 14 percent interest.
  • After three years with no redemption, the certificate holder has six months to start foreclosure.
  • Buyers pay $25 to register, and the county keeps $20 on each certificate sold.

The treasurer gives no legal advice to certificate buyers and points them to Nebraska statutes 77-1801 through 77-1941. If your own parcel is headed for the sale, talk with an attorney well before the last week.

Gather bids or photos for anything an inspector will flag, such as the roof, furnace or plumbing, and give the title company a list of open balances so the payoff is ready on signing day.

Owning a house that sits empty

With so many vacant units around the county, an empty house is not unusual here. It still costs money. The tax bill comes every year, and a freeze can burst a pipe in a home no one is watching.

Ask a neighbor or relative to look in regularly, keep payments current, and decide soon whether to list for months or to take a quick as-is offer. Cash buyers purchase in present condition, so a tired roof or an old furnace need not be repaired first.

Bank financing brings an appraisal, and an appraisal on a house needing work can derail a closing. Without a lender, those hurdles vanish and the calendar rests on the title search and on how quickly the tax payoff is confirmed.

The same obligations remain at the table: stamp tax, open tax balances, and the recorded deed. What shrinks is the waiting.

What to bring

Have your parcel number, photo ID and newest tax statement nearby for calls and visits. An heir should bring documents showing authority to sign. If the property is unoccupied, mention that to the title company at the outset.

If your parcel is headed for the March sale

Timing is the whole game here. The list is advertised in February, so by the time your name or parcel shows up in the paper, the sale is only weeks away. Paying the overdue amount before the first Monday of March keeps the parcel off the block. Selling before then works too, because the title company pays the delinquent tax from proceeds.

Ask the treasurer for a current figure, since interest keeps adding to the balance. Buyers at the sale cover later years' taxes as they come due, which means an investor with a certificate is tied to your parcel for up to three years.

May 1 for the first half and September 1 for the second.

Get a protest to the County Clerk by June 30, naming the value you want and your reasons. The Board of Equalization hears it, and the state commission handles further appeals.

The assessor, at 308-345-4388. The office is at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Strong evidence includes a recent appraisal, a contractor's estimate for repairs you have put off, and prices of comparable houses sold nearby. The same form covers a case where the assessor adds property that was omitted or imposes a penalty.

School districts and your bill

School levy follows the district. Columbus Public Schools (District 1) and Lakeview Community Schools (District 5) cover much of the area. Humphrey Public Schools (District 67) and Newman Grove Public Schools (District 13) serve the north and west. Twin River Public Schools in Genoa, Leigh Community Schools, Clarkson Public Schools, St. Edward Public Schools and Madison Public Schools also reach in.

Look for the district code printed on your statement before you compare your tax with a neighbor's.

Floods and older houses

Roofs, gutters and basement drainage take a beating in summer storms, and a house close to the Loup or Platte should get a flood check before it is listed. Flooding in 2019 reached Columbus. Put repair records, insurance claims and any elevation papers in a single folder, so a buyer's questions about water get quick, specific answers.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Platte County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

When taxes go unpaid

The county holds a tax sale every March for unpaid real estate tax. Investors buy the overdue amount as a certificate. They do not buy your house. Even so, a delinquent bill is more than a penalty: it starts a countdown. Pay the balance, or close a sale before sale day, and the exposure is gone.

Rules for the sale and the delinquent listing are on the treasurer's page, so you can check whether your parcel appears there.

Selling with taxes owed

Your first call should be to the treasurer for the balance on the parcel, because title companies insist that back taxes be cleared at closing. Next, set aside money for the deed tax. Nebraska's documentary stamp tax is the seller's to pay, the register of deeds collects it, and the rate is $3.32 on each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026. Form 521, the Real Estate Transfer Statement, goes in with the deed.

Typical sellers in this spot own an inherited house, a rental with a tenant, or a place with repairs half done. Buyers paying cash need no loan approval and no lender appraisal, which is why those closings can be quick. Send us the address if you would like a plain description of how a sale would go.

What to bring to the treasurer or title company

A modest folder spares you return trips: your parcel number, photo ID, older statements you still have, and proof of authority if an estate holds the house. With a mortgage in place, also request a payoff letter so the closing agent can add the tax balance and give you one clear total.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How a quick sale unfolds

Quick sales around Columbus and the smaller towns tend to follow one short path.

  • You give us the address and a few facts about the house, plus any tax or lien balance.
  • A buyer reviews the place and offers cash, with no bank in the middle.
  • The title company starts its search and asks the treasurer for the balance.
  • At the table you sign the deed and Form 521, and the stamp tax comes out of your proceeds.

With so few steps, the schedule follows title work and the speed of the tax payoff, not a lender's calendar.

Questions buyers ask here

Expect three. First, which school district the house is in, so have the district code from your statement in hand. Second, whether the lot has ever taken on water, which is why a folder of repair and insurance papers helps. Third, what the taxes run, and the best answer is last year's actual statement, not a guess.

A seller who answers these without hunting for papers keeps a buyer's attention and usually keeps the closing date too.

Frequently asked questions

When are Platte County property taxes due?

December 31. The first half is delinquent the following May 1 and the second half the following September 1, and late tax draws 14 percent interest.

Where do I file a Platte County valuation protest?

With the County Clerk in Columbus, on Form 422, on or before June 30. Each parcel gets its own protest with the reason, the value you want and supporting documents.

Can I pay Platte County taxes online?

Yes, through Nebraska Taxes Online. Mail and the courthouse drop box by the west entrance also work. Credit cards add 2.49 percent and debit cards $2.95.

What is the Platte County Treasurer's phone number?

402-563-4913. The office is at 2610 14th Street in Columbus, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Who pays the deed tax on a Platte County sale?

You do, as seller. The register of deeds takes the stamp tax when the deed is recorded, with a rate of $3.32 per $1,000 of value from July 18, 2026.

Washington County at a glance

Washington County sits in eastern Nebraska just north of Douglas County and the Omaha area, with Blair as the county seat. About 20,865 people live in the county. Most of the land is farmland, with Blair and Fort Calhoun as the cities and Arlington, Herman, Kennard and Washington as villages.

A homeowner here may live in a town, in a village or on a rural parcel, and that choice decides which municipal rules apply on top of the county's. Low ground near the Missouri River carries flood risk, as the 2011 river floods near the Blair bridge showed.

Selling in Blair or a village

Blair is the county seat, and the villages of Arlington, Herman, Kennard and Washington sit around it, with Fort Calhoun as the other city. A buyer will want to know which of these, or which rural parcel, the house belongs to, because that decides which municipal rules and levies apply. Because a cash buyer is not waiting on a lender's appraisal, farmhouses, inherited houses and homes with deferred repairs remain saleable.

Many Blair buyers work in the Omaha and Council Bluffs area, so commuting distance is a talking point. If the house sits on low ground near the Missouri River, tell the buyer before the inspection, since the 2011 flooding near the Blair bridge is part of the county's recent history and the lender may ask about flood insurance.

Before you list, collect the last tax statement, your protest paperwork if you filed one, and any homestead exemption confirmation. Then call the Treasurer at (402) 426-6888 for the balance and the Clerk at (402) 426-6822 if a protest is pending.

Sellers in Fort Calhoun or Kennard should expect the same paperwork as sellers in Blair, but the village or city may add its own rules for permits and nuisances. A short call to the clerk of your town before you list is cheap insurance.

Highways matter to commuters here: U.S. 30 and 75 and Nebraska 31, 91 and 133 all cross the county, and a buyer weighing a village against Blair will ask how long the drive to Omaha takes. Give an honest estimate, and mention which highway the house is closest to.

Which office does what

Four county offices touch a property owner, each with its own task.

OfficeWhat it doesHow to reach it
County AssessorSets valuations and reviews them before a protestCall the Assessor's office
County ClerkReceives Form 422 protests for the Board of Equalization1555 Colfax Street, Blair, NE 68008; (402) 426-6822; mail to P.O. Box 466
County TreasurerCollects real and personal property taxP.O. Box 348, Blair, NE 68008; (402) 426-6888
Register of DeedsRecords deeds and collects deed taxCall the Register of Deeds
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Washington County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How Nebraska values a home here

Values are set as of January 1. Houses, rural homes, buildings, commercial and industrial property, recreational property and mobile homes are held to 100 percent of market value, while agricultural land is held to 75 percent and priced from soil maps and land use such as dry, irrigated or grassland.

To get the bill, the county multiplies taxable value by the consolidated rate for your district, quoted per $100. A parcel in a town pays county, municipal and school levies together. That is why two houses of equal value can receive unequal bills when they lie in separate districts.

Notices and the homestead exemption

A changed value brings a notice from the assessor by June 1, addressed to the owner of record on May 20. Separately, qualifying owners may shield part or all of a home's value through the homestead exemption. File that application with the assessor between February 1 and June 30.

How to protest your valuation

A protest is made on Form 422 and filed with the County Clerk no later than June 30. Begin with a call to the Assessor's staff, since an explanation may make the protest unnecessary.

  1. Ask the Assessor's office to explain how they arrived at your value.
  2. File Form 422 with the Clerk by June 30. State the value you want, your reasons and the legal description, because a protest with no reasons can be dismissed.
  3. Request an Assessor review if you want one. A referee who is a registered appraiser may meet you before the Board of Equalization hearing.
  4. Go to the hearing. The Clerk sets the time and place and sends the Board's decision within seven days of the final action.
  5. Still unhappy? The Tax Equalization and Review Commission hears appeals made within 30 days of the Board's adjournment, and for the June 1 to July 25 session that adjournment is deemed to be July 25.

Protests cover valuation, never the tax rate. Comparable sales or a recent appraisal make the strongest case for a house. Personal property protests are due earlier, by May 1.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Washington County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

Real and personal property taxes are payable by December 31. Once that passes, the first half is delinquent on May 1 and the second on September 1. Interest on delinquent taxes owed to political subdivisions is 14 percent a year under Nebraska law. Douglas County uses different dates, so owners who moved up from Omaha need new reminders.

Send checks to the Washington County Treasurer, P.O. Box 348, Blair, NE 68008, or use the county's online payment vendor. Personal property tax becomes a first lien on everything of that kind you own as of the due date, and the property can be seized to satisfy it.

Tax sales

Nebraska Revised Statute 77-1801 links the county tax sale of delinquent real property to the first Monday of March. Statute 77-1802 has the county treasurer prepare a list of delinquent parcels four to six weeks ahead of that Monday. Back taxes on your house? Request a payoff figure from the Treasurer right away. More choices stay open, whether you pay, sell or negotiate, the earlier you know the total.

Selling with taxes owed

The title company usually takes any tax owed from your proceeds at the closing table and apportions the current year's bill between buyer and seller. A house with delinquent taxes can still close, since the payoff generally comes out of the price.

  • Phone the Treasurer at (402) 426-6888 for a balance before signing anything.
  • Request the title company's settlement statement ahead of signing day.
  • Make sure no earlier year remains open.

Country parcels need one more check. A rural property can lie in a different school or levy district from a house in town, so read the district on your bill before you quote taxes to a buyer.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording the deed

The Register of Deeds records county sales. Its fees are $10 for page one, $6 for every page after, and $1.50 a page for certified copies. Send a Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, with the deed.

The grantor owes Nebraska's documentary stamp tax of $3.32 on each $1,000 of value (fractions count) for deeds recorded July 18, 2026 or later. Plan for the state figure when you budget for closing.

Questions to ask before you sell

Which taxing district is the parcel in, and what did last year's bill look like? Has the assessor sent a notice of changed value, and was a protest filed? Is a homestead exemption in place? Is any personal property tax still open? Answering these before you call a buyer tells you what a closing will look like, and it lets you give a straight answer when the buyer asks about taxes.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Washington County, Nebraska property tax protest deadline?

For real property, file Form 422 with the County Clerk by June 30. Personal property protests are due by May 1. State the value you want and your reasons.

When do Washington County taxes become delinquent?

Delinquency follows the December 31 due date: after May 1 for the first half and after September 1 for the second. Interest runs 14 percent a year, and you can mail to P.O. Box 348 in Blair or pay online.

Can I sell my house in Washington County if I owe property tax?

Yes. Back taxes are normally paid from the proceeds at closing, and the title company confirms the payoff. Phone the Treasurer, (402) 426-6888, for a balance before you sign.

Who do I call to dispute my Washington County property value?

Talk to the County Assessor's office first. If the issue remains, file Form 422 with the County Clerk, 1555 Colfax Street in Blair, phone (402) 426-6822.

How is farmland valued compared with a house?

Houses are valued at 100 percent of market, while farmland is held to 75 percent and priced from soil maps and use.
